note: SNCF Intercités de Nuit, one entry per direction. SNCF's GTFS route names are not addresses — route_long_name is "-" (short name "INCONNU") for six of these trains, files Albi–Paris under "Paris - Latour-de-Carol" and Aurillac–Paris under "Paris - Rodez / Albi", and carries both directions plus the portions that split at Toulouse and Brive under a single route_id. So every entry is an oriented { from, to } pair, and `name` is Back-on-Track's own label for that direction — which is what the trainsByNumber enrichment looks a view-map row up by, so the feed's stop list lands on the row it belongs to rather than becoming a second copy of the route. `from`/`to` are the feed's station spellings ("Latour-de-Carol - Enveitg", "Nice-Ville"), matched accent-folded and prefix-wise. Day TGV and TER services that merely cross midnight are intentionally excluded, and buildSleeperTrains additionally requires a named entry's trip to run past midnight — the fullest Paris Austerlitz → Toulouse Matabiau trip in this feed is the 08:27 daytime Intercités via Limoges, which would otherwise have replaced the night train's Montauban routing under the night train's own number. Verified against the live feed by `probe-gtfs --verify-allowlists` (the 'Probe GTFS feed' workflow): the first run matched all 18 and returned 8–16 stops per train against Back-on-Track's 2–5. IC Nuit 3750/3751 are the two still under test — before the overnight rule they resolved to that day Intercités, so if the feed turns out to carry no overnight Paris↔Toulouse trip they will show up under "matched NOTHING" and should be dropped, leaving Back-on-Track's data in place.
